review_type: independent fresh-open, source-based and visual grade
name: Ward L. Lambert Fieldhouse and Gymnasium

criteria.evidence: The saved Purdue ArcGIS source feature is FID 261 (LAMB, Ward L. Lambert Field House & Gymnasium); the asset contains the named current GIS ground-footprint mesh. An independent projection of all 20 GIS vertices into the documented campus-local frame matches the asset footprint within 0.000002 m in both directions, with 0.0000014 m maximum bounding-edge error. The current Purdue Athletics page identifies Lambert Fieldhouse as its track-and-field home and states it contains a six-lane, 200-meter Rekortan track. The GIS polygon does not identify the archival hall/gym split or verify the exterior wall envelope.

The exported footprint matches the official GIS polygon within 0.000002 m; its bbox midpoint agrees with the documented local-coordinate anchor, and the lane-one track centerline independently measures 199.989 m. Purdue Archives evidence supports 303 x 172 ft for the fieldhouse and 210 x 110 ft for the gym; candidate dimensions are converted consistently. The archive does not georegister the historical plan rectangles against the present U-shaped GIS footprint, so fit and relative placement of the actual hall/gym volumes remain unverified.

criteria.criterion: Evidence-backed height, floors, and roof form
criteria.evidence: The cited Purdue Archives record supports a one-story fieldhouse and a separate four-story gym; the candidate has a broad arched fieldhouse roof and a lower flat gym roof. R9 explicitly labels the wall and roof heights as illustrative estimates. No measured elevations, roof section, truss spacing, floor-to-floor heights, or current roof profile are supplied, so the silhouette is plausible but not metrically confirmed.

I inspected the regenerated exterior and interior/event renders. The exterior depicts a broad arched hall roof, brick walls with repeated openings, pale vertical and horizontal detailing, and a glazed entrance; the interior shows a red six-lane track, seating, hurdles and high-jump equipment. Materials have surface variation and a packed brick image. Exact window rhythm, facade dimensions, entrance composition and current tower condition are not established by the sources; the model remains simplified and event equipment/interior layout is illustrative.

criteria.criterion: Modular export, portability, and complete evidence
criteria.evidence: A fresh Blender 5.2.3 LTS process opened the exact candidate SHA b15f99d5bd78b9f09f541f4fd26fa5286d7414034fb51583a62a2495299d36b7. Asset_lambert_fieldhouse contains 911 objects (906 meshes); every mesh has a material, the brick image is packed, there are no linked libraries, and the previously identified sidewalk/curb/road context meshes are absent. The candidate includes revision-specific evidence, validation, renders, and explicit uncertainty. The remaining 0.1 deduction reflects that this is still a candidate: placement at the master marker and fit against nearby campus context have not been independently checked in the full master.

evidence.summary: PASS; exact candidate SHA reopened with 911 exported objects, 906 meshes, no unassigned mesh materials, no linked libraries, one packed image, no site-context meshes, six-lane track centerline 199.988957 m.
